doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: Diva, Bria Skonberg and the Gully Low Jazz Band
summary: Women in college bands, Diva, and praise for Bria Skonberg and the Armstrong-dedicated Gully Low Jazz Band.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I mean that was it. And that wasn’t fair. Once in a while there would be somebody maybe in the trumpet section. And in the late sixties, early seventies, when was it, there was this really good lead trumpet player women, I think she’s still around. She eventually got some studio work and stuff. And she was a great lead trumpet player. And then you had Diva. That’s where I first heard Anat actually. She was one of the best people in that band. But it was really a hell of a band. It still is very good. I haven’t seen them in a while, but they could hold their own with quite a number of all male bands. They’re really a terrific band both in terms of section playing and soloing and so on. So women are becoming more recognized, as they are in general in the whole wide world. I mean now we have — suddenly we have business executives who are women. And if you watch television, which I do more now that I’m retired, although I am not a couch potato yet, but I do watch more. Like daytime TV, which I never watched before, it’s astonishing how many women there are on television as anchors, as reporters. Actually they outnumber the men. And they’re very good. They’re also good in things like reporting on the stock market like Maria Bartiromo and all these people, they’re very prominent. So women are definitely becoming more and more — and it’s true also in our environment in colleges and universities. Not only are there more female students, they are now pretty much the majority, but also faculty members and department chairs and so on. It used to be really dominated by men. So in the music too. There’s a really — have you hear Bria Skonberg yet?
Yeah. She’s cute. She’s from British Columbia.
Right. As a matter of fact I did see her, I almost forgot, at the Jazz Educator’s conference in Atlanta in January she was there.

She’s very good. And she is surprisingly, and it matters that way too, they can play anything. I mean she knows Louis backwards. There’s a band in New York that plays every Wednesday afternoon at Birdland from 5:30 to 7:15. It’s run by David Ostwald who is a lawyer who plays tuba, and it’s an Armstrong-dedicated band. It’s called the Gully Low Jazz Band. It’s a Louis Armstrong memorial jazz band. So they play all Louis repertoire. But Bria, she knows all the stuff, you know, she can do a terrific job on the cadenza to “West End Blues” you know. But even beyond that, I heard her a couple of weeks ago and she did “Cornet Chop Suey” and did it backwards. And then she can do very contemporary stuff. She writes songs and lyrics. She sings. She’s a very good singer. And it’s really nice to see. And Anat, can do that too. She plays with Ostwald too when she’s in town. She’s quite busy, you know, touring and stuff. And she can do the traditional clarinet stuff and then she can go outside too.
